To solve the inequality $P(x)>0,$ we need to find the values of $x$ for which the curve $y=P(x)$ lies above the $x$-axis.

First, we factorize the polynomial $P(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x) & ={x}^{4}-{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}({x}^{2}-x-2) \\  & ={x}^{2}({x}^{2}+x-2x-2) \\  & ={x}^{2}(x(x+1)-2(x+1)) \\  & ={x}^{2}(x+1)(x-2)\end{aligned}
$$

The roots of the polynomial $P(x)={x}^{4}-{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}$ are $x=-1,$ $x=0$ and $x=2,$ where

- $x=0$ has multiplicity $2,$ and

- $x=-1$ and $x=2$ are simple roots.

So, we can graph the curve as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14033945/assets/c0756761d00b0805683e447d8cee3b657bbbe004a0a47da428927585037b06c2.png)

Since we are interested in solving $P(x)>0,$ we look for the part of the curve that is above the $x$-axis.

Based on the graph, the solution is $x\in (-\infty ,-1)\cup (2,\infty ).$
